responsibility: Implements GCC’s target backend for the C-SKY architecture family, covering target configuration, option handling, ABI/runtime integration, instruction selection, and scheduling for both bare-metal ELF and Linux/ELF environments. The module’s central sources and headers define C-SKY-specific target hooks, calling-convention and register/addressing rules, builtin type and libfunc setup, and the architectural policies that guide RTL expansion and code generation, while the main machine description and its predicates and constraints encode the core integer instruction set, operand legality, PIC/TLS and constant-pool handling, and assembly output. Surrounding definition files describe the architecture/core/FPU feature taxonomy and generated -mcpu/-march/-mfpu option tables, and specialized .md families add DSP operations, shared and version-specific floating-point instruction sets including FPv2/FPv3 and half precision, plus per-core pipeline models for scheduler tuning. Driver headers and helper scripts complete the port by specifying linker/startfile/sysroot behavior and multilib selection, making this module the place where GCC adapts its generic middle-end and RTL backend to C-SKY ISA variants, ABIs, and microarchitectural characteristics.
